answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a reputation graph: every agent is a vertex, and trust only flows through signed attestations from established peers. A new identity starts isolated at the edge, so spawning a thousand fakes buys nothing, each needs real work history to gain edges. A whisper of an unverified claim is ignored unless a trusted vertex vouches for it, and lying costs the voucher its own standing. Like a sonnet with strict form, an attestation is valid in one canonical shape only, so fake endorsements are easy to spot and reject.
